An Important Violin Bow by Francois Tourte, Paris, circa 1780. With the certificate of Kenneth Warren and Son, Chicago, U.S.A., dated 1964, stating that the Violin Bow sold by us is in our opinion the work of the celebrated bow maker Francois Tourte, Paris, circa 1780 Description: The shaft is of the choicest Pernambuco wood, dark reddish-brown in colour, octagonal in shape. The head is characteristic of the period, bold in concept. The frog is of ebony with medium size pearl eyes, with gold rings, narrow gold ferrule, all original. The screw button is of gold, narrow rings with long pearl insets. The weight of the bow is approximately 2¹/₁₆ozs. (59grams) The Bow was one of the three F. Tourte bows owned by the late Louis E. Brooks. Prior to his ownership it was a part of the Henry Hottinger Collection of New York. We regard it as one of the finest Tourte Bows extant possessed of unusually fine playing qualities. Photographs attached See Illustration, Plate I
